_readme: Flagship pages to expand in place (pipeline step 3b — one per day, before the new article). Target 3,000–3,500 words, at least two data tables and one inline SVG figure, every threshold cited to an official source and the URL added to scripts/sources.json for the slug. Keep the existing URL, H1, schema types, answer box and FAQ (update, don't remove). Mark status 'done' with the date when finished.

items.brief: Currently 1,242 words on the site's most-linked page (Nomad Capitalist's equivalent is ~3,900 with 4 official links, 2 tables, 5 images). Add: (1) Investment routes table with the legal basis (Art. 90.º-A Lei 23/2007) — fund €500K (CMVM-regulated, 60% Portuguese companies, 5-year maturity), research €500K, cultural €250K (€200K in low-density), job creation — with government fee schedule (AIMA analysis/issuance/renewal fees, cite the Portaria) and typical legal/fund subscription cost ranges; (2) Fund due-diligence section: CMVM registration check, management/performance fees, lock-up and redemption, capital-guarantee myths, and the US-specific point that Portuguese funds are PFICs for US investors — Form 8621, QEF/mark-to-market elections, why this can wipe out the tax advantage; (3) Timeline figure (inline SVG): pre-approval → biometrics → card issuance → renewals, with the current AIMA processing reality and the 2025–26 backlog litigation; (4) Citizenship section rewritten around Lei Orgânica 1/2026 (10 years, transitional rules, language A2, clean record) and the 5-year permanent-residence alternative; (5) Family reunification; (6) Renewal cadence and the 7-day average; (7) Decision table GV vs D7 vs D8; (8) Refresh FAQ to 8 items. Sources: AIMA Portal ARI, AIMA FAQ, DRE consolidated Lei 23/2007, Lei Orgânica 1/2026 PDF, CMVM, IRS Form 8621 page.

Currently 1,392 words. Add: tier table by zone (€800K: Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and islands over 3,100 residents; €400K elsewhere; €250K for conversion of commercial buildings or restoration of listed buildings) with the 120 m² minimum and single-property rule (cite Law 5100/2024 and migration.gov.gr); the short-term-let ban on GV properties and its penalty; fee schedule; 5-year renewable permanent permit, zero stay requirement, no work; family scope; the tax side: no Greek tax residency without 183 days, ENFIA annual tax, rental income tax brackets, the non-dom €100K flat tax and 7% pensioner regime as pairings; US side: full worldwide tax, Form 1116 on Greek rent, FBAR on the Greek account; path to citizenship (7 years residence + language) is unrealistic without living there — say so. Add an inline SVG map/figure of the tiers and a cost worked example at €400K and €800K. Sources: migration.gov.gr, mitos.gov.gr, AADE.

Currently 1,595 words on the site's best-ranking page. Add: closing-cost table by state (ISAI 2–5% — cite state codes for Quintana Roo, Jalisco, BCS, Guanajuato, CDMX), notario fees, appraisal, SRE permit; the ejido-land and 'régimen de condominio' diligence checklist; pre-construction escrow reality; title insurance availability; condo HOA and short-let rules (state lodging taxes); mortgage options summary (link mortgage-in-mexico); residency pairing (link mexico-temporary-resident-visa once it exists); US tax summary linking us-taxes-property-mexico and selling-property-mexico-us-citizen; inline SVG 'restricted zone' figure (50 km coast / 100 km border); step-by-step timeline figure. Keep the fideicomiso section but shorten it and link the new /fideicomiso page when it exists. Sources: Ley de Inversión Extranjera PDF, Constitution Art. 27, SAT, INM, Rev. Rul. 2013-14.

Currently 1,364 words. Add: designated freehold areas list (cite Dubai Land Department / Regulation 3 of 2006), DLD 4% transfer fee and admin fees, Oqood registration for off-plan, escrow account law (Law 8 of 2007) and how to verify a project's escrow, RERA service-charge index, mortgage LTV caps for non-residents (UAE Central Bank regulation), AED 2M golden visa mechanics incl. mortgaged property rules (cite u.ae/ICP), rental yields by area with a source, DEWA and chiller charges, inheritance (DIFC Wills registry vs Sharia default), no UAE income/CGT/property tax and what that means for US tax (no credit — full US tax on rent and gains), corporate tax non-application to individuals. Two tables + one inline SVG (cost of purchase breakdown). Sources: dubailand.gov.ae, u.ae golden visa, icp.gov.ae, tax.gov.ae.

Currently 1,586 words. Add: per-country table (Portugal, Spain, Italy, France, Greece, Mexico, Dubai, Costa Rica, Panama) with typical non-resident LTV, term, rate basis (Euribor +), documentation, and whether US credit history counts — cite bank/central-bank sources where they exist and label ranges as market-typical; the currency-risk section with a §988 worked example; US deductibility of foreign mortgage interest (Pub 936 qualified residence rules); alternatives (US HELOC/cash-out, developer financing, cross-border lenders); the 'debt-service in a foreign currency' budgeting rule; and an inline SVG comparing a €300K purchase financed at 60% LTV vs cash over 10 years with a 10% dollar move. Sources: IRS Pub 936, 26 USC 988, ECB/central-bank pages for rates.

Currently 1,514 words. Add: who lends to foreigners (Mexican banks require residency/RFC; cross-border USD lenders and developer financing as the practical routes), typical MXN rates vs USD rates with a dated source, minimum down payments, the fideicomiso as collateral, closing timelines, prepayment rules, the §988 trap on a peso loan and the reverse (peso weakening = no deductible loss for a personal home), US deductibility (Pub 936), CONDUSEF as the regulator/complaints body, and a decision table: cash vs US HELOC vs Mexican bank vs developer financing. Inline SVG comparing total cost of the four routes on a US$300K purchase. Sources: Banxico, CONDUSEF, IRS Pub 936, 26 USC 988.
